lead: Fetal growth restriction is a fetus that fails to reach its growth potential from a pathological cause. SGA (weight below the 10th centile) is a size, not a disease: about two thirds of SGA babies are constitutionally small. FGR raises perinatal death 6–10 times.
f: SGA: below the 10th centile for gestation · FGR: pathological failure to grow · Low birth weight: under 2.5 kg at any gestation (two thirds preterm, one third SGA)

sc: EFW 8th centile, normal Doppler, small parents → Constitutional SGA

f: Symmetrical (20–30%): early onset; fetal cause (chromosomes, TORCH, drugs); HC, AC and FL all small; too few cells; poor outlook · Asymmetrical (70–80%): late onset; placental insufficiency (PE, HTN, malnutrition); AC small, head spared (raised HC:AC); abnormal Doppler, oligohydramnios; good catch-up if delivered in time

sc: All measurements small from 20 wk → Symmetrical FGR: karyotype, TORCH
AC small at 34 wk, mother has PE → Asymmetrical FGR

f: Maternal: malnutrition, anaemia, HTN, renal or heart disease, diabetes with vasculopathy, APS, smoking, alcohol, drugs, interval under 6 months · Placental (commonest): pre-eclampsia, abruption, praevia, infarcts · Fetal: trisomy 13, 18, 21; infection (CMV, rubella, toxoplasma, malaria); twins; anomalies · Poor placental flow → brain sparing → low liver glycogen (AC falls first) and less renal flow (oligohydramnios)
Early dating scan comes first · SFH lag over 3 cm or reduced movements → growth scan + umbilical artery Doppler · Low PAPP-A; uterine artery Doppler at 20–24 wk

sc: 32 wk, SFH 28 cm, mother hypertensive → Growth scan + umbilical artery Doppler

f: Growth scan: HC, AC, FL, EFW; AC is the best single measure; every 3 wk (shorter gives false positives) · Liquor: falling AFI · Umbilical artery Doppler: raised PI → absent → reversed EDF; normal = FGR unlikely · MCA: low PI = brain sparing; high peak velocity = fetal anaemia · Ductus venosus absent or reversed a-wave = acidaemia (late) · CTG · Cause: anomaly scan, karyotype if early or symmetrical, TORCH, BP

tr: Small baby + normal UA Doppler + normal liquor = usually constitutional SGA: do not rush delivery

f: Before birth: IUFD, hypoxia, fetal distress in labour, meconium aspiration · Neonatal: hypoglycaemia (low glycogen), hypothermia (little fat), polycythaemia (chronic hypoxia), hypocalcaemia, RDS, NEC, IVH · Long term: cerebral palsy, learning delay; Barker hypothesis (adult HTN, diabetes, heart disease)

sc: FGR newborn, 2 h old, jittery → Blood glucose

f: Treat the cause; stop smoking; treat malaria and anaemia · Kick chart, CTG, growth every 3 wk, UA Doppler weekly · Dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly × 4 if birth before 34 wk · SGA, normal Doppler: 39 wk (RCOG 2024; local 37–38 wk) · Raised UA PI with EDF present: by 37 wk · Absent EDF: by 34 wk · Reversed EDF: about 32 wk · Abnormal DV, pathological CTG or fast falling liquor: now · Normal Doppler: induction with continuous CTG; absent or reversed EDF: caesarean

sc: FGR 31 wk, DV a-wave reversed → Steroids + caesarean now
FGR 30 wk, absent EDF, CTG normal → Steroids, deliver by 34 wk

f: Paediatrician at birth, early feeding, glucose checks, warmth, check PCV · Prevention: early booking and dating, stop smoking, treat anaemia, malaria and HTN · Low-dose aspirin from 12 wk if high risk of placental disease · Interpregnancy gap over 6 months
